summary: Nebraska National Forest lookout: first tower 1916, present third tower 1944; 2022 Bovee Fire destroyed or damaged the cab; viewable, not enterable.

facts.status_note: The tower still stands, but the cab was destroyed or damaged in the October 2022 Bovee Fire. Accounts differ, and renovations were under way as of March 2025.

access.note: Grounds open year round, 24/7. The tower can be visited and viewed but not entered.

visit.trail_note: From Thedford, take Highway 2 about 17 miles east, then turn south onto State Spur 86B and follow it about 3 miles to a loop around the tower. Parking is to the right of the tower.

events.note: First tower on the site, per NHLR.
Present tower, described by NHLR as the third on the site.

Bovee Fire, October 2022. NHLR says the cab was destroyed; a news report says the fire destroyed the tower; Wildfire Today and the Forest Service say it was damaged and the steel framework still stood.
Forest Service page, last updated March 28, 2025, says the site is undergoing renovations.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Accounts of the October 2022 Bovee Fire differ. A news report says the fire destroyed the tower. NHLR says the cab was destroyed. Wildfire Today and the Forest Service describe damage, and Wildfire Today says the steel framework still stood. The record is kept as standing with a status note, and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Brief said status standing; kept, with a status note for the cab loss. The 1944 date comes from NHLR only. A Forest Fire Lookout Association post seen in search (not fetched, so not cited) gives 1973 for the current third tower; check before changing the 1944 date. Elevation: NHLR 2,907 ft (886 m); Forest Service page shows 2,922 with no unit. Height 50 ft is from one news report. No staffing source found, so staffing is omitted. Photos on the NHLR page have no captured URLs; none added.
